title: Electrochemical Cells
short_title: galvanic cells, E° values, electrolysis and corrosion
standard_text: Electrochemistry: electrochemical (galvanic) cells, standard reduction potentials and cell voltage, electrolytic cells and electrolysis, batteries, and corrosion. (summary of BC's Curriculum, Chemistry 12)
meta_desc: Free Chemistry 12 worksheets (BC Curriculum): galvanic cells, E° values, electrolysis and corrosion. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Galvanic cells make electricity from spontaneous reactions.
key_sub: Oxidation at the anode, reduction at the cathode.
body_html:
How to think about it

In a galvanic (electrochemical) cell a spontaneous redox reaction produces electricity. Oxidation happens at the anode and reduction at the cathode; electrons flow through the wire and ions through the salt bridge. E°cell = E°cathode − E°anode.

In an electrolytic cell an outside power source drives a non-spontaneous reaction, as in electroplating and making aluminum. Corrosion is the unwanted oxidation of metals; it can be prevented by painting, galvanizing or cathodic protection.

Example

E°(Cu²⁺/Cu) = +0.34 V and E°(Zn²⁺/Zn) = −0.76 V. What is E°cell?

0.34 − (−0.76)

Answer: +1.10 V

Example

At which electrode does oxidation occur?

An Ox

Answer: the anode

Common mistakes

  • Thinking electrons flow through the salt bridge.
  • Getting the sign of E°cell wrong.
  • Thinking electrolysis is spontaneous.

faq.q: Why is zinc used to galvanize steel?
faq.a: Zinc is oxidized more easily, so it corrodes instead of the iron.

faq.q: What does a salt bridge do?
faq.a: It lets ions flow to keep each half-cell electrically neutral.

items.q: A cell is made from the 2H⁺/H₂ (E° = 0 V) and Ag⁺/Ag (E° = 0.800 V) half-cells. Which half-cell is the negative electrode?

items.q: Which product forms at the negative electrode (cathode) during electrolysis of aqueous sodium chloride (brine)?
items.e: Molten: the metal forms. Aqueous: hydrogen forms unless the metal is less reactive than hydrogen.

items.q: Dilute aqueous sodium chloride is electrolyzed with inert carbon electrodes. What is formed at the cathode (negative electrode)?
items.e: Positive ions go to the cathode. In aqueous solutions of reactive metals, hydrogen is discharged instead of the metal.

items.q: Aqueous potassium iodide is electrolyzed with inert carbon electrodes. What happens at the anode (positive electrode)?
items.e: Negative ions go to the anode. In dilute solutions OH⁻ is discharged (oxygen); concentrated chloride gives chlorine; a copper anode dissolves.

items.q: Molten lead(II) bromide is electrolyzed with inert carbon electrodes. What happens at the anode (positive electrode)?
items.e: Negative ions go to the anode. In dilute solutions OH⁻ is discharged (oxygen); concentrated chloride gives chlorine; a copper anode dissolves.

items.q: Concentrated hydrochloric acid is electrolyzed with inert carbon electrodes. What happens at the anode (positive electrode)?

items.q: Which product forms at the positive electrode (anode) during electrolysis of aqueous copper sulfate?
items.e: Halide ions give the halogen; otherwise oxygen forms.

items.q: In 2FeCl₃ + H₂S → 2FeCl₂ + 2HCl + S, which is the reducing agent?
items.e: H₂S loses electrons (is oxidized), so it is the reducing agent.

items.q: What is the role of a salt bridge?
c: it completes the circuit and keeps the solutions electrically neutral
items.e: Usually KCl or KNO₃ in agar.

What is the sum of oxidation numbers in a neutral compound?
c: equal to the charge on the metal
items.e: In an ion it equals the charge.

items.q: What happens to the molar conductivity of a solution when it is diluted?
items.e: Ions move more freely.

items.q: What happens to the conductivity (κ) of a solution on dilution?
items.e: There are fewer ions per unit volume.

items.q: In 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO, which is the reducing agent?

Which pair of metals gives the largest voltage in a simple cell?
items.e: The further apart the metals are in the reactivity series, the larger the voltage.

items.q: What is a fuel cell?
c: a cell that converts the energy of burning a fuel such as H₂ directly into electricity
items.e: Used in the Apollo space program.

items.e: FeCl₃ (Fe³⁺) gains electrons (is reduced), so it is the oxidizing agent; H₂S is the reducing agent.

items.q: In Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂, which is the reducing agent?

items.q: In a simple cell made of aluminum and copper, in which direction do electrons flow in the external wire?
